interpretation: Static nodewise information was insufficient, but full edge topology was not necessary for single relational targets.
First-passage, intervention response and critical-node count each collapsed the four topology worlds into only three target classes and required one relational measurement in every row.
A single first-passage measurement was the canonical minimum not only for first-passage itself but also for intervention and critical-node-count targets in this controlled topology family.
Pairwise relation structure required two measurements in every row, canonically one REL bit plus one FP depth.

The combined relation + first-passage + intervention suite required two measurements but induced four target classes in every row, thereby refuting Q7: asking all relational questions together recovered full topology identity across the four archetypes.
Target-specific compression is therefore strongest when the ecological question is narrow; combining multiple relational targets can eliminate the compression advantage.
claim_boundary: Unit measurement counts are conceptual information counts rather than real sampling costs.
Cross-family sufficiency is conditional on the v10 four-topology archetypes and labeled-node design.
Q7 remains refuted: the combined relational suite did not leave topology identity unresolved.
The result motivates target-specific relational summaries rather than one universal connectivity statistic.
